title: SEP-IRA vs Solo 401(k) for the self-employed: 2026 limits
label: Year-end tax move

items.s: About 20% of your net self-employment earnings.

items.t: Open and fund it by your tax deadline

beats.text: No employees? A 401(k) can still be *set up*
beats.sub: By the filing deadline, extensions not counted.

cta.sub: We'll DM you our year-end planning page.

captions.instagram:
Self-employed and want to put money away for retirement before filing? Two common choices, with 2026 limits:

✔️ SEP-IRA: business contributions only, about 20% of your net self-employment earnings. You can open and fund it up to your tax deadline, including extensions.
✔️ Solo 401(k): up to $24,500 as the 'employee' ($8,000 more at 50 or older), plus a business contribution, up to $72,000 total before catch-up.
✔️ Owners with no employees can set up a 401(k) after Dec. 31, by the filing deadline (extensions don't count).

Which one fits depends on your income. Our year-end planning page has the other deadlines.
